title: Probability: Venn Diagrams and Tree Diagrams
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Probability Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use mutually exclusive and independent events when calculating probabilities; link to discrete and continuous distributions; use Venn diagrams and tree diagrams.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on probability: P(A ∪ B), mutually exclusive and independent events, and tree diagrams with and without replacement. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
body_html:
How it works

Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together: P(A ∩ B) = 0. Independent events: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B). On a tree diagram, multiply along the branches and add the outcomes you want.

Example

P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, independent. P(A ∩ B)?

0.5 × 0.4

Answer: 0.2

Common mistakes

  • Adding probabilities that are not mutually exclusive.
  • Forgetting to change the second probability without replacement.
  • Multiplying for 'or'.

faq.a: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.

faq.q: How do you test for independence?
faq.a: Check whether P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).
